mcqs.learning_point: Understand the meaning of parallel lines
mcqs.question: Which of the following statements about parallel lines is NOT true?

options.A: Parallel lines are always the same distance apart.
options.B: If extended far enough, parallel lines will eventually intersect.
options.C: Parallel lines lie in the same plane.

mcqs.answer: If extended far enough, parallel lines will eventually intersect.
mcqs.explanation: Parallel lines, by definition, never meet no matter how far they are extended; therefore statement B is false. Statements A, C and D correctly describe properties of parallel lines.

mcqs.question: Line l passes through (1,2) and (3,6). Line m passes through (2,3) and (4,7). Are the two lines parallel?

options.D: It cannot be determined from the given points.

mcqs.explanation: The slope of line l is (6‑2)/(3‑1)=2. The slope of line m is (7‑3)/(4‑2)=2. Equal slopes mean the lines are parallel, so option A is correct.

mcqs.question: Figure I shows two straight lines that run in the same direction and never meet. Figure II shows two straight lines that cross each other. Which figure contains parallel lines?

options.C: Both Figure I and Figure II
options.D: Neither Figure I nor Figure II

mcqs.explanation: Parallel lines are lines that never intersect. Figure I meets this condition, while Figure II shows intersecting lines. Hence only Figure I contains parallel lines.

mcqs.learning_point: Recognise parallel lines in everyday surroundings
mcqs.question: Which of the following pairs of objects are examples of parallel lines?

options.A: The opposite edges of a rectangular notebook
options.B: The two sides of a triangle
options.C: The edges of a book cover that meet at the spine
options.D: The lines of a road that appear to meet at the horizon

mcqs.answer: The opposite edges of a rectangular notebook
mcqs.explanation: Opposite edges of a rectangle are straight, lie in the same plane and never meet, satisfying the definition of parallel lines. Options B and C are not parallel, and option D describes converging lines, not parallel.

mcqs.learning_point: Understand the meaning of parallel lines
mcqs.question: Parallel lines are lines that:

options.B: Never meet, no matter how far they are extended

mcqs.answer: Never meet, no matter how far they are extended
mcqs.explanation: The defining property of parallel lines is that they do not intersect, regardless of how far they are prolonged. The other options describe different relationships.

mcqs.question: Which pair of lines below are parallel?

options.A: Two lines that cross each other
options.B: Two lines that lie on top of each other
options.C: Two lines that never meet and run in the same direction

mcqs.answer: Two lines that never meet and run in the same direction
mcqs.explanation: Parallel lines are straight, lie in the same plane, have the same direction, and never intersect. Option C matches all these criteria.

mcqs.question: In a diagram, which statement correctly distinguishes parallel lines from intersecting lines?

options.A: Parallel lines intersect at a single point.
options.C: Parallel lines have the same slope, while intersecting lines have different slopes.

mcqs.answer: Parallel lines have the same slope, while intersecting lines have different slopes.
mcqs.explanation: Equal slopes indicate parallelism; different slopes indicate that the lines will meet at some point. The other statements are false.

mcqs.learning_point: Recognise parallel lines in everyday surroundings
mcqs.question: Which of the following everyday examples shows a pair of parallel lines?

options.A: The two rails of a railway track
options.B: The sides of a V‑shaped road sign
options.C: The edges of an opened book
options.D: The two sides of a triangular road sign

mcqs.answer: The two rails of a railway track
mcqs.explanation: Railway tracks are designed to be straight and remain the same distance apart, fulfilling the definition of parallel lines. The other options involve lines that meet or are not straight.
